description:
Design and implement a tmux workflow inspired by iTerm/Zellij with a toggleable right-side overview.

Terminology
- tmux session: the whole attached workspace, usually named after the project directory. A session contains windows.
- tmux window: the tmux equivalent of a Zellij tab or iTerm tab. A window contains panes.
- tmux pane: a split terminal inside one tmux window. Panes are the leaf terminals where shells/editors run.
- Sidebar: a special right-side tmux pane used only for navigation/status. It is not counted as a normal work pane in the displayed list.

Goal
Add a right sidebar that can be shown/hidden by command. The sidebar lists all windows in the current session. Under the active/current window, it lists that window's panes vertically. The active window and active pane must be visually obvious.

Initial UX
- Default state: sidebar hidden, normal tmux layout.
- Toggle command: one binding should show the sidebar if hidden and hide it if visible. Preferred binding: prefix + b or Alt-b, unless that conflicts with another important workflow.
- Hide command: the same toggle should remove the sidebar and restore the remaining work panes to usable width.
- The sidebar should be narrow and predictable, around 28 columns to mirror the Zellij sidebar layout.
- Sidebar should sit on the right edge of the current tmux window.
- Sidebar should update when windows/panes are created, closed, renamed, or focused. A short polling interval is acceptable if hooks are too brittle.

Sidebar Content
- Header: current session name.
- Windows: list window index + window name for every window in the session.
- Active window marker: visually distinguish the active window.
- Panes under active window: list pane index, active marker, current command, and a shortened current path if practical.
- Empty/missing names should fall back to stable tmux IDs or indexes.

Interactions
- Minimal first version can be read-only. Navigation by clicking/choosing is optional for a later ticket.
- If interaction is simple, allow selecting a window or pane from the sidebar using tmux commands, but do not block v1 on this.
- Sidebar pane should not be accidentally killed by normal pane cleanup if possible; if it is killed manually, the toggle command should recreate it cleanly.

Implementation Constraints
- Prefer tmux-native scripts and bindings over a heavy plugin.
- Do not require Zellij.
- Do not break existing prefix C-s workflow.
- Do not steal important existing bindings without an explicit choice.
- Sidebar should avoid recursive behavior: the sidebar pane itself must not appear as a normal pane in the pane list.
- Keep implementation in the dotfiles repo, likely under tmux/ plus a small executable helper script.

Open Design Questions
- Should the sidebar be per-window or per-session? Proposed: per-window visually, but showing session-level windows and active-window panes.
- Should the sidebar be persistent across all windows, or recreated per active window? Proposed: start per-current-window because tmux panes are window-local.
- Should clicking/selecting items be supported in v1? Proposed: not required for v1.
- Should hidden/restored layout preserve exact pane sizes? Proposed: best effort; avoid complex layout persistence until needed.

Acceptance Criteria
- A documented binding toggles the right sidebar on and off.
- When shown, the sidebar appears on the right and does not replace the active work pane.
- Sidebar lists all windows in the current session.
- Sidebar lists panes for the active window underneath that window.
- Active window and active pane are clearly marked.
- Creating/closing/renaming windows or panes is reflected in the sidebar without restarting tmux.
- Hiding the sidebar leaves normal work panes usable and does not kill user work panes.
- tmux config validates with source-file after the change.
title: Add tmux right-side window and pane overview
